checks: Merging two coordinates of equal height preserves scalar height. A splitting interval of length λ_i and the density ratio N!/(N-1)! give likelihood Nλ_i with no simplex-volume convention loss.
The larger height list has N+1 coordinates, so its density factor is N and its truncated power exponent is m. Multiplying by V/N produces exactly the displayed moment formula.
The Fubini equality of densities extends at interior and extreme knots by compact-convex slice continuity, with bounded affine barycentric integrands. In a zero-volume limit the moment tends to zero.

The integrated affine barycentric expansion gives both sum identities and the sampled centroid. Convexity puts the centroid in C, so admissibility is exactly its base integrality. Source §3 and exact replay agree.
